## Deciding which side to do it on

The choice, made explicitly and with reasons, between joining server-side and bringing geometry back to `sf`. Both work. This example should pick one, say why, and note what the other would have cost, since the reader's situation may differ.

## Setting the CRS

Geometry arrives as WKB with no embedded SRID, so `st_srid` returns 0 and the number has to come from you. The failure mode is what makes this worth a section: a missing CRS does not error, it produces wrong areas or a join that matches nothing.

## The join itself

## Checking the result is plausible

Row counts before and after, and an eyeball plot. A join that silently matches nothing looks exactly like a join that matched everything, in the shape of the output.

## Confirming the two sides agree

The server-side answer against R's, on a sample, as described in [Check that you get the same answer wherever it ran](../howdoi/check-the-answer.qmd). This is where the recipe there gets its second, structurally different case, which is what that page currently lacks.
